_purpose: Framework-required keys for a consumer's .claude/settings.json. That file is _skip_if_exists (it holds consumer permissions), so copier update can never deliver a framework settings change on its own. sync-from-core and auto-sync read this manifest after copier update and reconcile the difference. This file IS CORE and does update.

_classes.managed: Framework owns the VALUE. Reconciliation overwrites a differing value and reports the change at Notice tier. These encode framework posture, not consumer preference.
_classes.additive: Framework owns only the DEFAULT. Reconciliation adds the key when absent and never touches a value the consumer already set.
_classes.never_write: Reconciliation MUST NOT write these under any circumstance, in any tier, for any reason. Never-automate invariant 1 (credential/access grants). A missing or wrong value here is surfaced to the human as a Confirm-tier prompt and applied only on their approval.

_rationale.agent: Makes chief-of-staff the main-thread agent so the steward posture is loaded as a system prompt rather than hoped for from prose. Before this key existed in a scaffold, routing to the steward was a single paragraph in a consumer-owned CLAUDE.md that a competing user-level instruction could and did override.
_rationale.enabledPlugins.claude-code-sdlc@claude-c: OPOS repos have their own execution model. Running the SDLC pipeline alongside it produces two competing answers to 'what do I do first' and the steward loses. Scoped to this project only; other repos on the machine are unaffected.
_rationale.hooks.SessionStart: Scheduled routines registered on the claude-schedule runtime are session-scoped and die on session exit; the first entry prints a re-arm reminder. The second (v0.16.0) mints this session's identity for the lease protocol and prints one line of current occupancy read from the committed projection — zero API calls. Additive because a consumer may have their own SessionStart hooks worth preserving. KNOWN HOLE: because this class never overwrites a value the consumer already set, a consumer that already has a SessionStart array does NOT receive the second entry automatically; `sync-from-core` reports it and the consumer appends it by hand. The third (v0.19.0) is the daily in-session OPOS updater: once a day per clone it starts a background job that gets any newer OPOS release applied and fast-forwards the clone, and prints one line only when something happened. Consumers that already have a SessionStart array must append it by hand (the same additive-class hole described above); `sync-from-core` reports it.
_rationale.hooks.UserPromptSubmit: Fires right before the next expensive turn, which is the last point a warning can still change what that turn does — a SessionStart hook only fires once, at the start, and says nothing about a session that grew large mid-conversation. context-budget-notice.mjs is fail-open (every step wrapped, always exits 0) and silent unless a new context-size band was just crossed, so it costs nothing on a healthy session. Additive, and safely so: unlike SessionStart (which most scaffolds already populate, so the additive class's 'only when absent' rule leaves the second SessionStart entry undelivered to existing consumers — the KNOWN HOLE noted above), a consumer without a UserPromptSubmit key yet is the common case, so this hook reaches it automatically on the next settings reconciliation.
_rationale.autoCompactWindow: Verified at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config (settings key `autoCompactWindow`, accepted range 100k-1M; default on a 1M-context model compacts at ~967k) and confirmed present as `--autocompact` in `claude --help` on CLI 2.1.280. 250000 keeps sessions out of the measured 400k-925k band where 81% of one real session's 244M tokens were spent, well before the ~967k default would ever trigger. Managed as `additive` (not `managed`) so a consumer who has deliberately set their own value keeps it.
